moneyline.label: Moneyline
moneyline.note: Model log loss 0.682 against the actual posted prices on all 1,414 holdout games, the market's 0.679 -- statistically level. But backing the model's side at those prices returned -8.1% per dollar. Shown for context, not to bet into.

puckline.label: Home -1.5
puckline.note: The sharpest game-level market here: it removes 2.79% of the base rate's error against the moneyline's 1.81%, and all seven probability bands land inside their intervals. It used to sit three points low; a trailing-window level correction now closes that.

sog_15.label: Over 1.5 shots
sog_15.note: Best market available: 13.3% of baseline error removed, and beats a player's own average at t=8.3.

sog_25.label: Over 2.5 shots
sog_25.note: 13.2% of baseline error removed, t=5.6 vs a player's own average.

saves_245.label: Over 24.5 saves
saves_245.note: Removes 5.7% of the base rate's error, under half what shots on goal manage. Its value is the baseline it beats: a goalie's own recent average is worse than guessing the league mean, because past save counts reflect the opponents he faced.

saves_275.label: Over 27.5 saves
saves_275.note: Removes 5.6% of the base rate's error. The calibration slope of 1.31 means the quoted probabilities are, if anything, too cautious.

saves_305.label: Over 30.5 saves
saves_305.note: Removes 4.6%. The thin end of the distribution: fewer starts reach it, so the estimate is noisier, though every band lands inside its interval.

sog_35.label: Over 3.5 shots
sog_35.note: Removes 10.3% of the base rate's error against 13.3% at the lower lines. Slightly weaker and in the tail, but properly calibrated.

dog.why: the model is backing the side the market has as the underdog; it won 47.6% of 212 such games, but underdog prices pay more, so the return was +0.4% with an interval of plus or minus 14 points -- not established either way

thin.why: the model's confidence is under 60% and the market agrees on the side; 758 such games returned -12.8% per dollar with the whole interval below zero, and the 171 of them that showed an edge returned -13.7%. This is the one situation established as a loser

fav.why: a strong favourite the market also favours; 444 such games returned -1.8%, and the 204 that showed an edge returned +2.7% with an interval of plus or minus 11 points -- the only positive sign anywhere, and still indistinguishable from zero
